notes:
Account background: Lakehaven is a national freight & last-mile logistics operator (1k+ employees). Exploring Redwood Dedicated + Private control plane to replace current multi-cloud model. Procurement is accelerating—board sign-off contingent on strict uptime + meaningful credits.

Sales/AE notes (Maya): initial POC in Q4 2025 validated functional parity for reranking model and chat assistant. POC load patterns: morning batch (06:00-09:00), two steady daytime peaks, nightly batch. They care about sustained throughput for embeddings jobs (search indexing) and low p99 latency for chat/rerank.

Key technical asks from infra/ops:
- Throughput guarantee: baseline reserved GPUs sized for sustained 2000 concurrent chat sessions and 10k embedding units/day; planning doc attached.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 250ms for short chat prompts (<=128 tokens), p99 < 800ms; for heavy rerank jobs p95 < 800ms.
- Reserved GPU planning: want dedicated pool per region (NA-east, NA-west, EU) with hot standby.

SLA negotiation specifics discussed on calls:
- Lakehaven ask: 99.99% availability monthly for dedicated pools.
- Redwood draft: 99.9% standard for Dedicated; credits begin at monthly availability <99.9. Lakehaven pushing for steeper credit schedule and cap removal.
- Proposed credit schedule (Lakehaven counter-proposal): 5% monthly credit for availability 99.9-99.7, 15% for 99.6-99.0, 35% for <99.0; request special carve-out for prolonged incidents >8h that impact more than one region.
- Maintenance windows: Lakehaven requires maintenance to be scheduled in 02:00-04:00 local region or with 7-day advance notice and cross-region routing during maint. No one-off maintenance during seasonal peaks (Q4 freight peak).
- Support response times: Lakehaven requests P1 response <30 minutes and 4-hour remediation SLT (or escalation to on-call eng). Redwood standard: 1-hour P1. Also ask for dedicated Technical Account Manager during onboarding + 24/7 escalation channel.

Quotes from stakeholders: 'We cannot afford cross-region downtime during Q4; credits are a hygiene factor but runbooks and routing guarantee uptime.' — Head of Infra.

Legal procurement notes: need to align on indemnity, data residency clause for EU customers, and KMS key control for certain EU routes. Procurement team requested a redlineable SLA PDF and sample SOC2 report.

Open technical questions: acceptable burst capacity policy (auto-burst costs), exact definition of "availability" for multi-pool config, SLA measurement probes/URLs, impact of scheduled maintenance on availability calculation.

Action items: attach new SLA draft (v2) w/ updated credit tiers, deliver technical appendix describing probe endpoints and measurement, schedule legal markup meeting (Maya + Redwood legal + Lakehaven counsel).
